title: Hazard and Risk Register
purpose: Identifies the work health and safety hazards of the organisation's work, assesses the risks they create, and records the controls chosen by the hierarchy of control, their owners and how they are reviewed — consulting the workers who do the work.

questions.text: Which of these hazard areas apply to the work? Tick only what applies — each ticked area becomes a confirmed starting point for the register; add anything else under Other.

items.label: Electrical risks and energised electrical work
Plant and structures, including mobile plant
Psychosocial hazards — from how work is designed or managed, the work environment, plant, or workplace interactions and behaviours
Principal mining hazards at a mine the organisation works at (for example ground instability, inrush, roads and mobile-plant areas, fire or explosion)
items.note: identified and managed by the mine operator; the organisation works within those controls

questions.text: Which risk rating method does the organisation use?
How are the workers who do the work consulted when hazards are identified and controls chosen?
When is the register reviewed (for example after an incident, a change, or new work)?

requiredSections: Register of hazards, risks and controls
Controls by the hierarchy of control
Link to the risk and opportunity register and emergency plan
optionalSections: Task-based risk assessments (for example safe work method statements) referenced from the register
expectedRecords: Inspection and review records showing controls are checked
draftingRules: Table columns: ID | Task or area | Hazard | Risk | Inherent rating | Controls (by the hierarchy) | Residual rating | Owner | Review date.
Build rows only from the ticked areas, the confirmed hazards and the answers. Where nothing is confirmed, leave a placeholder row — never invent hazards.

Controls follow the hierarchy of control as the Safe Work Australia code cited describes: eliminate first; then substitute, isolate or use engineering controls; then administrative controls; then PPE.
Cite a regulation part only where its hazard area is ticked.
reviewerChecklist: Every hazard traces to real work or a ticked area
Controls follow the hierarchy of control
Each control has an owner and a review date
Mine-site work reflects the mine operator's requirements

sources.title: Etcher ISO gap analysis workbook V2.0 — evidence examples (column G)
Work Health and Safety (General) Regulations 2022 (WA) — official consolidation
Work Health and Safety (Mines) Regulations 2022 (WA) — official consolidation
Model Code of Practice: How to manage work health and safety risks (November 2024)

brandingInstructions: Use the organisation's confirmed legal or trading name in the header, its logo reference (describe where the logo goes — do not invent one) and its confirmed brand colours for headings and table header rows. Put the document-control block in the footer or on a cover table. If a branding value is not confirmed, leave a placeholder.
